entries.result: Firearm-homicide IRR 1.08, 95% CI 1.03 to 1.13; main national model, Results.
entries.breadth: 41 states, 23 statutory adopters and 18 controls, 1999 to 2017; monthly state rates. Observational controlled interrupted time series, not randomized. State associations differ.
entries.access: Full article and RAND review read.
entries.conversion: size = IRR - 1; range = published main-model 95% IRR interval minus 1. This interval measures pooled-estimate uncertainty, not variation across states.
entries.transportLimit: Study excluded nine states and does not establish effects for territories, townships, newer enactments, repeal, or preempted local rules. State variation can exceed this pooled interval. No legal authority is inferred.
entries.readerStatus: No person feels this yet: no cause or outcome reader was verified in this research batch. A numeric entry is not runtime activation proof.

entries.result: Page 26: inverse-sampling-error-weighted IV elasticity 0.45. Pages 20 to 21 report 0.3 to 0.6; page 27 reports 0.6 to 0.7 near the regulatory cutoff.
entries.breadth: US monitored counties, 1971 to 1972 changes induced by Clean Air Act nonattainment. TSP, not PM2.5 or an air-quality index. Outcome is internal-cause infant deaths per live births.
entries.access: Working paper full text and tables read.
entries.conversion: size = 0.45 / 100; range = [0.3 / 100, 0.7 / 100]. The cause is percent of starting TSP, so a one-point increase gives a 0.45% local proportional mortality increase.
entries.transportLimit: Study specification/subsample spread is not a CI or modern PM2.5 coefficient. Requires TSP-specific cause and infant internal-cause outcome readers; neither was verified. No supported general air-quality-index conversion.
entries.readerStatus: No person feels this yet: no cause or outcome reader was verified in this research batch. A numeric entry is not runtime activation proof.
entries.per: one percentage-point increase in TSP concentration relative to place start; local linear elasticity approximation near start

entries.result: Table 5 two-step GMM elasticity -0.344, SE 0.096; one-step -0.348, empirical likelihood -0.344.
entries.breadth: US cities, 1960 to 2010; annual growth in sworn officers and crime; within-state comparisons.
entries.access: Working paper full text and Table 5 read.
entries.missingFigure: Need each place's officer-density baseline and a verified transformation from percentage growth in officers to the existing officers-per-1000 diminishing shape. The table elasticity is not a coefficient per additional officer per 1000. Confirm final cited version and timing before sizing.

entries.result: Table 5 two-step GMM elasticity -0.174, SE 0.062; one-step -0.178, empirical likelihood -0.173.
entries.breadth: Same city panel and specification as violent-crime entry.
entries.access: Working paper full text and Table 5 read.
entries.missingFigure: Need each place's officer-density baseline and the percentage-growth-to-officers-per-1000 conversion for the existing diminishing shape. Confirm final cited version and timing; -0.174 is an elasticity, not a per-density-unit size.

entries.result: Author abstract reports more quality-of-life arrests and disproportionate impacts on Black Americans; no numerical low-level arrest coefficient is supplied in the abstract.
entries.breadth: Race-specific US police-force study; cannot substitute the older crime-elasticity paper.
entries.access: Author abstract read; Europe PMC full-text endpoint returned HTTP 500.
entries.missingFigure: Need the low-level arrest estimate and reported uncertainty by race, observation period, and conversion from an additional officer to the runtime density input. Full table remains unread.

entries.result: Author abstract: 43% fewer violent-crime arrests over 16 months; 3.95 fewer arrests per 100 assigned youth.
entries.breadth: Randomized assignment of 1634 disadvantaged Chicago high-school youth to an eight-week program; mostly post-program decline.
entries.access: Author abstract read.
entries.missingFigure: Need assignment-effect interval, eligible-youth denominator, program take-up, and the slot-to-assignment mapping. A raw extra slot is not a 43% reduction for the whole place, and assignment is not treatment received.

entries.result: Table 4 fully controlled 2SLS: release -0.156 probability points, SE 0.034; detained mean 0.571.
entries.breadth: Marginal defendants affected by randomly assigned bail judges in Philadelphia and Miami-Dade; release versus detention.
entries.access: Working paper full text and Table 4 read.
entries.missingFigure: Need the final AER table interval, conviction baseline among the affected marginal defendants, and a defined detention input unit. Reversing a release effect and dividing by the whole detained mean does not establish the effect of detention on every defendant.

entries.result: Table 7 fully controlled 2SLS: release +0.037 employment probability points (SE 0.043) in years 1 to 2, +0.102 (SE 0.053) in years 3 to 4.
entries.breadth: Same marginal defendant population; tax-record formal employment, not all work.
entries.access: Working paper full text and Table 7 read.
entries.missingFigure: Need final published estimates and intervals, affected-defendant employment baseline, and distinct follow-up exposure records. The first-period imprecise estimate is not evidence of zero; a single immediate lag cannot represent both periods.

entries.result: Author abstract: Medicaid nearly eliminated catastrophic out-of-pocket medical expenditure approximately two years after the lottery.
entries.breadth: Oregon low-income lottery applicants; clinical follow-up samples 6387 selected and 5842 not selected. Coverage effect estimated using lottery assignment.
entries.access: Author abstract read; Europe PMC full-text endpoint returned HTTP 500.
entries.missingFigure: Need catastrophic-expenditure control mean, coverage-effect estimate, its reported interval and exact income-denominator definition from the financial table. Nearly eliminated supplies no numeric range; general coverage is not necessarily this Medicaid benefit.

entries.result: Table V: first-year shelter-use IV +0.034 (SE 0.017), non-evicted mean 0.009; second-year -0.001 (SE 0.013). Cook County first-year +0.023; New York +0.046.
entries.breadth: Adults in filed cases, Cook County and New York; judge-assignment IV. Shelter use is not all homelessness.
entries.access: July 2023 working paper full text and Table V read.
entries.missingFigure: Need final QJE table and interval, mapping from orders to affected adults, and measurement of homelessness outside shelters. A shelter-use effect cannot be copied into a generic homelessness rate; no supported two-year persistence of the first-year shelter coefficient.

entries.result: Table VIII: first-year non-pregnancy hospital visits +0.188 (SE 0.094), non-evicted mean 0.739; second-year -0.113 (SE 0.142).
entries.breadth: New York adults in filed eviction cases; judge-assignment IV; quarters after filing.
entries.access: July 2023 working paper full text and Table VIII read.
entries.missingFigure: Need final QJE estimates and intervals, affected-adult denominator and exposure unit, and first-year versus later-year records. The introduction rounds to 0.19 visits and reports 29%; dividing 0.188 by the unconditional non-evicted mean is not necessarily the paper's complier effect.

entries.result: Table 3: turnout-share coefficients 0.021, 0.022, 0.021, with SE 0.009, 0.007, 0.008.
entries.breadth: County rollout in California, Utah and Washington, 1996 to 2018; general-election turnout divided by citizen voting-age population.
entries.access: Full article and Table 3 read.
entries.missingFigure: Need each place's matching citizen-voting-age turnout baseline and denominator agreement with voting.turnout-pct. The reported 2.1 to 2.2 percentage points are additive; runtime size multiplies a base rate. It is not a 2.1% relative increase.

entries.result: Author abstract: strongest effects within a week among African-American children, about -0.5 SD vocabulary and -0.66 SD reading.
entries.breadth: Children ages 5 to 17 in Chicago; timing relative to nearby homicide; replicated with a second Chicago dataset.
entries.access: Author abstract read; Europe PMC full-text endpoint returned HTTP 500.
entries.missingFigure: Need outcome-specific coefficients and intervals by exposure window, score standard-deviation-to-runtime-score mapping, and decay estimates. Vocabulary and reading effects are not lower and upper bounds for one outcome.

entries.result: Table 5 nonattainment coefficients on TSP change: -11.9, -11.0, -10.0, -8.8, -8.9, -6.3 micrograms per cubic meter across specifications.
entries.breadth: 1972 nonattainment designated using 1970 TSP relative to the federal ceiling; US monitored counties, one-year change.
entries.access: Correct Chay and Greenstone working paper and Table 5 read.
entries.missingFigure: Need exposed-place initial TSP concentration and actual nonattainment eligibility/enforcement to convert the absolute concentration change into a proportional outcome factor. A general emissions law is not automatically this designation. No invented national percentage cut.

entries.result: Table 3 main controlled prematurity coefficient -0.0086 probability points, SE 0.0034. Table 4 restricted five-kilometer comparison -0.0064; time-trend specification -0.0074.
entries.breadth: E-ZPass adoption; mothers within two kilometers of toll plazas versus farther comparison mothers.
entries.access: Working paper full text and Tables 3 to 4 read.
entries.missingFigure: Need the congestion input's measured E-ZPass-equivalent dose and matching premature-birth baseline. Specification spread is not a confidence interval, and the abstract relative reduction is not a coefficient per raw congestion unit. Confirm final cited version.

entries.result: Table 4: ten-microgram-per-cubic-meter TSP increase yields -186.21 to -351.74 annual earnings dollars across specifications; log-earnings coefficients -0.005 to -0.014.
entries.breadth: Birth cohorts 1969 to 1974 in 148 counties; earnings ages 29 to 31; Clean Air Act IV.
entries.access: Working paper full text and Table 4 read.
entries.missingFigure: Need final JPE estimates, earnings price year and matching cohort mean for the annual-earnings outcome, plus birth-year TSP units and exposure record. Log earnings and mean annual earnings are different estimands; the log coefficients cannot silently replace the annual-earnings outcome.

entries.result: Working-paper abstract: sustained 10% higher spending in all 12 school years adds 0.27 completed years, 7.25% wages, and lowers poverty 3.67 percentage points.
entries.breadth: US school-finance reforms; cohort school exposure; larger effects for low-income children.
entries.access: Working paper full text read.
entries.missingFigure: Need final QJE attainment coefficient and interval (existing anchor says 0.31), exposed-pupil spending baseline, completed-school-years baseline, and all-12-year exposure mapping. A one-year raw dollar increase is not the sustained intervention.
entries.per: 10% more every year for 12 years: +0.31 years

entries.result: RAND fifth-edition review: supportive evidence of reductions in youth firearm suicides, homicides or assault injuries, and unintentional injuries/deaths for specified child-access laws.
entries.breadth: Definitions distinguish storage/child-access and reckless-provision laws; age and outcome definitions vary.
entries.access: Current RAND policy review read.
entries.missingFigure: Need matched law-definition estimates and intervals separately for youth suicide, homicide and unintentional death, with ages and follow-up. Evidence grades supply no pooled numeric range for a combined youth gun-death outcome.

entries.result: RAND fifth-edition review: supportive evidence that minimum purchasing-age laws reduce youth firearm suicide.
entries.breadth: Purchasing versus possession ages and covered firearm types are distinct; youth age definitions differ.
entries.access: Current RAND policy review read.
entries.missingFigure: Need the specific age transition, firearm coverage, youth age band, reported suicide estimate and interval, and lag. A generic minimum-age yes/no does not identify the treatment whose size was studied.

entries.result: RAND fifth-edition review: supportive evidence that shall-issue laws increase firearm homicides; permitless and may-issue rules are distinct comparisons.
entries.breadth: US state laws with different issuance and eligibility rules.
entries.access: Current RAND policy review read.
entries.missingFigure: Need the exact permitting transition and firearm-homicide estimate/interval for that comparison. A permit-required boolean combines shall-issue and may-issue laws; simply reversing a shall-issue estimate would misidentify the treatment.
